topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Etiological Foundations, Risk Factors, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and micro-evolutionary disease and explore how endogenous errors, inherited traits, and environmental exposures drive cancer patterns across global populations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a key case study of pathogen-driven oncogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, UV radiation, cigarette smoke compounds, and industrial chemicals undergo metabolic processing to cause DNA adducts, oxidative stress, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and the role of host tissue developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the laboratory, genomic, epidemiological, and toxicological approaches used to measure carcinogen exposure, test mutagenicity, and evaluate cancer risks.
